chunks.heading: Updating the Icemoor vault
chunks.text:
After each game session you add the session notes to the vault. The scripts in this folder then do the bookkeeping:

- They tidy up the new session note: file name, date and title line.
- They record who and what each session mentions, so the Dataview tables in Obsidian stay current.
- They refresh the **Session history** box at the bottom of every person, place, faction, item and quest note.
- They rebuild the campaign dashboard, a web page you can open in any browser.

Everything happens in one step. You don't need to know any programming.

---

chunks.heading: Part 1: One-time setup
chunks.text: You only do this once per computer.

chunks.heading: Step 1. Install Python
chunks.text:
Python is the free program that runs the scripts.

**On a Mac**

1. Go to **python.org/downloads** and click the yellow **Download Python** button.
2. Open the downloaded file and click through the installer, accepting the defaults.
3. When it finishes, a Finder window opens. Double-click **Install Certificates.command** in it. It's harmless and avoids problems later.

**On Windows**

1. Go to **python.org/downloads** and click the yellow **Download Python** button.
2. Open the downloaded file. **Before clicking Install, tick the box "Add python.exe to PATH"** at the bottom of the first screen

chunks.heading: Step 1. Install Python
chunks.text:
n.exe to PATH"** at the bottom of the first screen. This is the step people most often miss.
3. Click **Install Now** and wait for it to finish.

Any Python version 3.8 or newer works.

chunks.heading: Step 2. Find your vault folder on your computer
chunks.text: This is the folder Obsidian opens. It contains `Sessions`, `People`, `Places` and so on, plus this `scripts` folder. In Obsidian you can find it by right-clicking any note and choosing **Reveal in Finder** (Mac) or **Show in system explorer** (Windows).

chunks.heading: Step 3. Install the script requirements
chunks.text:
The scripts don't need any extra packages right now, so you can skip this step. If someone adds a package to `scripts/requirements.txt` later, this is how to install it:

1. Open a terminal *in the vault folder*:
   - **Mac:** in Finder, right-click the vault folder and choose **New Terminal at Folder**. If you don't see it, open the **Terminal** app, type `cd ` (with a space after it), drag the vault folder onto the window, and press Return.
   - **Windows:** open the vault folder in File Explorer, click in the address bar at the top, type `cmd` and press Enter.
2. Type this and press Return/

chunks.heading: Step 3. Install the script requirements
chunks.text:

2. Type this and press Return/Enter:
   - Mac: `python3 -m pip install -r scripts/requirements.txt`
   - Windows: `py -m pip install -r scripts\requirements.txt`

chunks.heading: Step 4 (Mac only). Allow the update shortcut to run
chunks.text:
The first time you double-click **Update Vault (Mac).command**, macOS may say it "can't be opened" or comes from "an unidentified developer". If so:

1. Click **Done** or **Cancel**.
2. Right-click (or Control-click) the file and choose **Open**.
3. Click **Open** in the box that appears.

macOS remembers this, so from then on a plain double-click works.

---

chunks.heading: Step 1. Add the session note
chunks.text:
In Obsidian, create a new note in the **Sessions** folder and paste in the session write-up. Start the note with the session number and date on the first lines, as you already do:

```
Session 39
8 October 2026
Riffle bursts into Talir's office to explain...
```

You can name the note `Session 39` or `Session_39`; the script fixes the name either way. Don't add a header or metadata yourself; the script writes them.

chunks.heading: Step 2. Link the names (recommended)
chunks.text:
The vault knows a person, place or quest is in a session only when its name is a link. To link a name, type two square brackets `[[` and start typing it. Obsidian shows a list of matching notes; pick one and it becomes `[[Talir Rengavi]]`.

- **To keep the wording you wrote**, add a vertical bar after the name: `[[Theo'din Corvis|Theo]]` shows as "Theo" but links to Theo'din's note.
- **For someone new**, link the name anyway. The link shows faded because there's no note yet; click it and Obsidian creates the note. Put new notes in the right folder (People, Places, and so on).

You don't have

chunks.heading: Step 2. Link the names (recommended)
chunks.text:
lder (People, Places, and so on).

You don't have to link everything before running the update. The update lists the names it found that aren't linked yet (see Step 5).

chunks.heading: Step 3. Add a short recap (optional)
chunks.text:
Add two lines like this just below the date lines (or, once the update has run, just below the title line it creates):

```
> [!summary] TL;DR
> Riffle defends themself to Talir while Deanira and Theo find a staircase under the Owens mausoleum.
```

Obsidian shows this as a recap box, and the dashboard uses it as the session summary. Without it, the dashboard shows the session's first two sentences instead.

chunks.heading: Step 4. Run the update
chunks.text:
Pick whichever is easiest:

- **Mac:** open the `scripts` folder in Finder and double-click **Update Vault (Mac).command**.
- **Windows:** open the `scripts` folder in File Explorer and double-click **Update Vault (Windows).bat**.
- **From a terminal** (opened in the vault folder, as in Part 1, Step 3): type `python3 scripts/update_all.py` on a Mac or `py scripts\update_all.py` on Windows, then press Return/Enter.

A window opens and reports its progress. It finishes in a few seconds with **All done**.

chunks.heading: Step 5. Read the "Things to check" list
chunks.text:
If anything needs your attention, the window lists it before "All done". For example:

```
Things to check in Obsidian:
  • Session 39 has no TL;DR recap (the dashboard will show its opening lines instead)
  • Session 39 mentions but doesn't link: Furgus, Hana Goldfirm, Samuel Patel
```

Fix what you want to fix in Obsidian, then run the update again (Step 4). Running it more than once is always safe.

The list only covers new sessions and the latest one, so it won't nag you about old sessions. It deliberately ignores names that are also ordinary words, like Tiny, Queen or Wolf, so check those

chunks.heading: Step 5. Read the "Things to check" list
chunks.text: ry words, like Tiny, Queen or Wolf, so check those yourself.

chunks.heading: Step 6. Look at the dashboard
chunks.text:
Open the `dashboard` folder in the vault and double-click **Icemoor Dashboard.html**. It opens in your web browser and shows:

- the latest session's recap
- the open threads, and when each last came up
- a grid of who appears in which session
- a searchable session log
- a directory of every note

If it was already open, refresh the browser tab.

The online copy Claude published is a separate snapshot. Ask Claude to republish it when you want that copy updated too.

chunks.heading: Step 7. Save to GitHub
chunks.text:
Commit and push the changes the way you normally back up the vault. The update changes the new session, the metadata blocks and history boxes of affected notes, and the dashboard file.

---

chunks.text:

chunks.heading: What the scripts change, and what they leave alone
chunks.text:
- **Metadata block** (between the `---` lines at the very top of a note): the scripts rewrite only their own fields. On every note those are `type`, `status`, `first_seen`, `party_member`, `location_type` and `item_type`. On sessions they also rewrite `session`, `date`, `previous_session`, `next_session` and the lists of linked people, places, factions, quests and items. Anything else you put in the block stays.
- **Session history box:** fully rewritten each time, between the `%% session-history:start %%` and `%% session-history:end %%` markers. Don't write inside those markers, because your

chunks.heading: What the scripts change, and what they leave alone
chunks.text:
s. Don't write inside those markers, because your text would be replaced. Everywhere else in a note is yours.
- **Your own writing:** never changed. The only exception is a brand-new session note, which gets its title line and metadata added the first time.
- **Nothing is ever deleted.** A new session file may be renamed (for example `Session_39.md` to `Session 39.md`). Obsidian doesn't notice renames made outside it, so if you already linked to the old name somewhere, change that link to the new name.

chunks.heading: Changing who's in the party
chunks.text:
The party list sits near the top of `update_metadata.py`. Open that file in any plain text editor (TextEdit on Mac, Notepad on Windows) and find these two lines:

```
PARTY = {"WISC", "Furgus", "Deanira", "Riffle", "Philip", "Theo'din Corvis"}
PCS = {"WISC", "Furgus", "Deanira", "Riffle", "Philip"}
```

`PARTY` is everyone who travels with the group. `PCS` is the player characters only. To add someone, put their note name in double quotes, separated by a comma, exactly as the note is named. Save the file and run the update.

---

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
**"python3: command not found", "'py' is not recognized", or the window closes immediately**
Python isn't installed, or on Windows the "Add python.exe to PATH" box wasn't ticked. Re-run the Python installer, choose **Modify**, and make sure that option is on. Then restart the computer.

**Mac says the .command file can't be opened**
See Part 1, Step 4.

**"Session_39.md and Session 39.md are both session 39"**
There are two notes for the same session. Combine them into one in Obsidian, delete the other, and run the update again.

**"can't tell the session number from the file name"**
The scrip

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
the session number from the file name"**
The script found a file in `Sessions` whose name doesn't contain a number. Rename it to something like `Session 39`.

**A session's title has no date ("no date found in the first lines")**
Put the date on the first or second line, written like `8 October 2026`, and run the update again. If the note already has its title line, just fix the date in the title line (`# Session 39 — 8 October 2026`) and the `title:` line in the metadata block above it.

**"Something went wrong and the update stopped partway"**
Nothing was deleted. Copy the whole message from

chunks.heading: If something goes wrong
chunks.text:
*
Nothing was deleted. Copy the whole message from the window and send it to whoever helps with the vault (Claude can read it too).

**The dashboard didn't change**
Refresh the browser tab. If you opened the dashboard from GitHub or Claude, that's a different copy; open the file in your vault's `dashboard` folder instead.

> Goliath raiders ambush them, and one, [[Uthal]], defects with intel on [[Ilkan]]'s camp. The party scouts the camp and plans a pre-dawn attack.


We are fired upon by 5 goliaths. During the fight, one of the archers turns on the other warriors and says he’ll join us and offer information on the camp. He wants vengeance. We see that he’s covered in bruises in various stages of healing, and he’s telling us the truth. [[WISC]] and [[Furgus]] disarm him and we talk. He says his name is [[Uthal]]. He tosses [[Deanira]] some nice bandages. He tells us that there are another doze

chunks.heading: Session 11 — 6 August 2025
chunks.text: bandages. He tells us that there are another dozen goliaths in the region, scattered between different raiding parties and the camp. [[Ilkan]] is the new leader. [[Uthal]]’s father used to be the tribal leader. They weren’t raiders, but were nomads and herders. [[Ilkan]] came back one day, smarter. He kept coming up with new ideas like contraptions to improve their chances and better ways to make it through the [[Tryborne Pass|Triborn Pass]]. [[Ilkan]] killed [[Uthal]]’s father and took over leadership of the tribe. They now have a Druid named [[Alkan]] who is often sent out as a hawk or owl

chunks.heading: Session 11 — 6 August 2025
chunks.text:
[[Alkan]] who is often sent out as a hawk or owl to scout. We remember that the previous night we heard the hoot of an owl. That’s how they found us. [[Ilkan]] keeps [[Uthal]] alive and in servitude as an insult to his father’s name. A little less than a day’s travel up the mountain is the camp.
He says that a little while back they found a caravan with fine rum and cigars, so at night many of them drink, which could be to our advantage. After [[Uthal]] kills [[Ilkan]], he wants to return to being a nomad and working for people as a herder.
With regards to strategy, we plan to attack at night

chunks.heading: Session 11 — 6 August 2025
chunks.text:
th regards to strategy, we plan to attack at night, when the Goliaths can’t see well and are likely drunken (mechanically the poisoned condition). We are considering having [[Uthal]] go to the camp and tell them they need help with loot so that, so that they peel off from the main camp and we pick them off at a choke point we create at the bottom of the path.
We head to the camp. When we arrive, it’s twilight and the residents are beginning to light the fires and open casks of rum. [[Riffle]] sends their familiar to scout and get a lay of the land. 3 big guys, 3 archers, 1 sleeping Druid, and

chunks.heading: Session 11 — 6 August 2025
chunks.text:
and. 3 big guys, 3 archers, 1 sleeping Druid, and 1 leader. 4 tents are
also there and perhaps occupied. The Druid is close to the boss, and the boss is not drinking.
The Plan:
We plan to take a long rest now, wake up around 0400 when it’s still dark, when they’re drunk, asleep, and can’t see in the dark. As we make our way up into the camp, we will systematically take out the braziers. We will first take out the two closest to the log so we have the cover of darkness. We’re hoping that Rifle can command the two guards to flee, since we can’t one shot them.

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> [[Hambrick Onyxcrest]] dispels the stone, revealing a giant "onion" of layered spells. The party hears of the [[Anthracite Trade Mystery|anthracite price hike]], takes a job clearing the grain route, and gains the horse Dante and the [[Grey Bag of Tricks]].


Anita: [[Riffle]]
Taylor: [[WISC]] Dhruv: [[Furgus]]
As we walk into [[The Warhammer]], [[Gunther Rockhammer]] waves us over. He says that he has work for us. The city has been receiving many complaints from shipments being ambushed. They have a large grain shipment coming in soon that absolutely needs to be delivered

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text: ming in soon that absolutely needs to be delivered to the city so they can make it through the winter. They want us to eliminate any raiders we find. We’ve been told by [[Oswald]] Sulter (Cuban who was ambushed) at [[Unfinished Business]] that parties have been ambushed by Goliaths. The grain shipment comes in in 3 weeks, they need the route cleared by then. We agree to take the job and head out in a day or two after the market and after we talk to the wizard who has returned from the Feywild luncheon. He invites us into his study which is lavishly decorated. He serves us breakfast platters an

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text: shly decorated. He serves us breakfast platters and cappuccinos and we sit and tell him about the stone. He inspects it and casts a 6th level dispel magic on it, and it bursts. The stone became as large as the table and crumpled it beneath it. The wizard tells us that this is an “onion”, an item with layers and layers of spells on it, usually created by people to conceal what the object truly is. You need to use many high level spells in order to reveal what the item truly is. He asks us to leave it with him for a little while while he tries to find out more about it and break some of the spel

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text:
find out more about it and break some of the spells. We oblige. We head to the monthly market and buy a tent of glamping, a tanning kit, and [[Riffle]] gets some basic poisons. At the market, we notice a quiet but heated conversation between two Dwarves, and they mention mithril and anthracite (a type of coal predominantly mined by the [[Black Hand Dwarves]] of Kohlenmine. It is an extremely hard coal that burns extremely hot for an extremely long time. It is necessary for forging mithril and
adamantine). Based on the conversation, the [[Black Hand Dwarves]] have more than doubled the price o

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text:
Hand Dwarves]] have more than doubled the price of the anthracite. The Dwarves of [[Truemetal Halls]] ask what the deal is, as they’re the only buyer. The [[Black Hand Dwarves]] respond that it’d their own business if they have another buyer.
We head out to clear the trade route for the grain shipment, when we see a black horse grazing on the side of the road. It’s fully tacked and has splotches of red on it. The blood is dried, and doesn’t seem to be the horse’s. When [[WISC]] walks up, he smells death. [[Riffle]] goes through the saddlebags and concludes that the rider was a courier.
They p

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text:
and concludes that the rider was a courier.
They pocket the letters and look into the supply pouch, where the food is beginning to go Bad. [[WISC]] looks around and ends up finding a dead human with blows to his head. A tree branch has blood on it as does a rock on the ground. We conclude that he was riding and hit his head on the branch, fell, and hit his head on the rock and died. We now have a fully tacked horse. [[Deanira]] names it Dante. [[WISC]] finds an empty gray bag and pulls from it a giant badger. He reaches in again twice more and pulls out two giant rats. [[Riffle]] recognises it

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text:
pulls out two giant rats. [[Riffle]] recognises it as a [[Grey Bag of Tricks]]. He relates what the item is in the narrator’s voice (Mike). [[Riffle]] suggests that we use them as scouts, sending one in front of us and one to each side to scout for danger. We agree this is a great idea. We set up the tent of glamping and sleep for the night. It goes by peacefully. The next day we’re walking and feel rain, but it doesn’t look like it’s raining. It’s red. [[Deanira]] looks up and gets hit by the head of a giant elk, dropped by a white dragon flying north.
[[Deanira]] harvests the antlers and sto

chunks.heading: Session 10 — 22 July 2025 Lyra: Deanira
chunks.text:
ng north.
[[Deanira]] harvests the antlers and stores them in the bag of holding. As we walk, a cloud of arrows descends upon us.

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> [[Riffle]] joins after pickpocketing and copying the journal. The party meets [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]], who tells them the legend of Axeholm and agrees to crack the cipher. Deanira keeps his silver dildo as collateral.


Lyra: [[Deanira]] Taylor: [[WISC]] Dhruv: [[Furgus]]
We decide to spend the day exploring the city, as the monthly market isnt for two days. As we’re walking through, Dwarves are hanging banners, one of which is on a ladder. He falls and cracks his head open. As we run over, a luxuriously robed kenku runs over as well. They are exquisitely decorated in gold

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text:
er as well. They are exquisitely decorated in golden rings and other jewellery. [[Deanira]] and the kenku examine the man, he is not breathing and portions of brain have come out, very clearly dead.
The foreman tells us his name was Daggen. The undertaker arrives and takes care of the body. The kenku turns and waddles over to [[Junk in the Trunk]]. We follow them to try to recruit them to our party. They are about to buy two books when [[WISC]] walks up and puts his paw on the books and offers to pay for them. We begin to talk. They are looking for historical books and secrets. They also like

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text: for historical books and secrets. They also like things that are shiny and things that are soft. They are wearing a clerical pendant of a lit candle dripping onto a stylized eye. They tell us that their deity is Deneir. We offer them to read the journal that we found on the dead Halfling suspended from a rope in the cave. They’re able to pick out of the cryptics “[[Axeholm]]”. I metagame and randomly say the name “[[Daddy Dildo Daggins]]”. The shopkeep replies, “oh you know [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]]?” He tells us that [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]] stayed a dragon and then became incredibly wealthy. H

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text:
yed a dragon and then became incredibly wealthy. He then became a collector. The last time the shopkeep saw him he gave him a package that he ordered. It was a little while ago, and he wouldn’t disclose what it was. The kenku vanishes and pickpockets the journal, unbeknownst to us. We go on a hunt for fish sticks (it’s unsuccessful). Riﬄe goes to a coffee shop and copies several pages of the journal (the page before, the [[Axeholm]] page, and the following page.)
The rest of us finish shopping and head back to [[The Warhammer]] for the evening. Meanwhile, Riﬄe asks the Barista if they know whe

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text:
Meanwhile, Riﬄe asks the Barista if they know where Mr. [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]] lives. She says he lives on this (upper middle class) ring of the city, but she’s not sure quite where. He used to adventure with others, so they may know.
Back at [[The Warhammer]], the three of us are chatting about a job that the Alchemist offered to us via [[Furgus]]. He is offering an advance of healing potions, and 100 gold each upon return of ingredients. We are to pick up ingredients and return them to the apothecary.
Apparently the road has bandits. Soon after, Riﬄe comes up to us and hands us back the jo

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text: fter, Riﬄe comes up to us and hands us back the journal, implying that we dropped it, but we are wise to it. We pretend it was a test. They introduce themself, their name is the sound of rifling paper from books in a library. We translate this to Riﬄe. We discuss [[Axeholm]] and Riﬄe suggests we sneak into [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]]’s home and rifle through his things to find a lead to [[Axeholm]]. They know that it’s an ancient Dwarven city, very, very deep underground, though they’re not sure where. [[WISC]] asks the waitress where he lives and she gives us directions. “It’s an oddball house, b

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text: she gives us directions. “It’s an oddball house, but you can’t miss it.” We make our way towards the house and come upon a hobbit hole into the outer wall, complete with a garden of grass and flowers and a Pickett fence. [[WISC]] and [[Deanira]] go up to knock on the door to talk to [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]], while Riﬄe and [[Furgus]] will sneak into the house and look around. We mention our interest in his landscaping but he sees right through it. We sigh and mention [[Junk in the Trunk]] and he mentions that he just received a package from them. He says it’s for his “personal collection”. He i

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text:
. He says it’s for his “personal collection”. He invites us in to see. We enter a lavishly furnished study filled with dildos. He is convinced they are all male fertility statues from various cultures. [[Furgus]] and Riﬄe “go to the bathroom” while we remain engaged in conversation with [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]]. [[Deanira]] expresses interest in cartography and exploring ancient Dwarven cities. He said that the crowing jewel of his collection would be the solid gold jewel encrusted statuette of [[Axeholm]]. It’s NW of [[Truemetal Halls]], ruled by the Axeforge family.
The town grew very wealthy

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text:
by the Axeforge family.
The town grew very wealthy because of the gold and jewels mined from there. Queen Sylvie commissioned this golden jewel-ribbed dildo to be created. One day a supernatural greed set upon the city. One day the royal family discovered a large portion of the treasure was missing, along with a number of the guard and royal [[Court]]. They sealed off the city until the culprit was found. At that time, a legendary blizzard came upon the city and buried the entrance. We show him the journal and he says that he wants to work on it for a few weeks to crack the cipher. [[Deanira]]

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text: t for a few weeks to crack the cipher. [[Deanira]] offers to seek out [[Axeholm]] to find the golden dildo for him. He said that he would provide any research and leads he’s collected over the years. He would pay very handsomely. [[Deanira]] asks if Dwarven worship of the god of greed Abathor could have contributed, he says it’s possible. We leave the journal with him for the next few weeks and [[Deanira]] takes the silver dildo as collateral. After we leave, [[Deanira]] hears a voice in her head, one she hasn’t heard since her first visit to the city. “This is Kilston Whistlebelt, assistant t

chunks.heading: Session 9 — 17 July 2025 Anita: Riﬄe
chunks.text: he city. “This is Kilston Whistlebelt, assistant to [[Hambrick Onyxcrest]], my Master (the wizard) is home and is willing to meet with you tomorrow to look at the mysterious magical object you inquired about.” We agree to meet tomorrow about the stone.

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> The Emberstones reward the party with [[Reaper]], a chromatic quiver and thunderous handwraps. [[Lord Ivan Deepshaft]] of the [[Court]] debriefs them on the mine in secret and asks them to keep quiet; the city pays 900 gold for the information.


Upon our return to the city, we visit a new magic shop that has just opened and is still in the process of unpacking, called [[The Shooting Star]]. The proprietor, a gnome with light pink fuzzy hair and the deepest voice we’ve ever heard, Mr. Bubblegum, greets us. He isn’t able to identify what our stone is. We see a few items we’

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
identify what our stone is. We see a few items we’d like to buy eventually.
We sell our dire [[Wolf]] pelts to a leather shop, and she recommends that we attend the market to get a tanning setup, a skinning knife, and salt to cure the pelts. They will then be worth 10 gold each in a decent condition.
We then go to the War Hammer and the owner [[Gunther Rockhammer]] calls us over. He gives us a letter that came for us. It’s from the desk of [[Earl Emberstone]]. Thanking us for the safe return of his son, inviting us to the [[Ring of Gold]] to collect our reward.
We head to the [[Ring of Gold]]

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
llect our reward.
We head to the [[Ring of Gold]] where we are presented with gifts. [[WISC]] receives a spectacular bill hook with a Raindrop Damascus pattern called “[[Reaper]],” forged by the [[Iron Dwarves]]. [[Furgus]] receives a quiver made of a quilt of chromatic dragon skins, embedded with magical properties. [[Deanira]] receives linens embedded with runes of gold. They are the thunderous handwraps, once worn by a monk dedicated to the god Kord.
When we return to the War Hammer, [[Gunther Rockhammer]] tells us that per our request our belongings have been moved to Room 10. We don’t rec

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
elongings have been moved to Room 10. We don’t recall requesting this. We go to the room and see a nicer room with cozier looking bar stools, and noticeably no bed. Out of the shadows, we see a Dwarf step out. He removes his mask and introduces himself as [[Lord Ivan Deepshaft]]. He says he’s a member of the [[Court]] and understands that we recently came across some things that would be beneficial for them to know, like what we discovered in the mineshaft. We share what we learned, but
[[Deanira]] doesn’t offer the map, and we don’t mention Abathor. We share that the Duergar are using the kno

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
athor. We share that the Duergar are using the knockers to mine mithral for the army they are raising. When we mention [[Elzock Emberstone]]’s capture, we see the slightest flicker of a smirk cross his face. [[Deanira]] gives him her “mithril” dagger pendant and we tell him that the Duergar believe they are doing this for a higher power and the Knockers appear to also worship this figure. As we prepare to leave, Lord Ivar tells us to not share what we discovered in the mines, in order to avoid a panic and allow the [[Court]] to resolve it quietly.
We go back downstairs and for the first time,

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
ly.
We go back downstairs and for the first time, [[Gunther Rockhammer]] motions for us to sit down at the booth with him. He says that it seems we have helped out several high powers in the city today. He hands us a leather pouch and informs us that the city will be paying for our room and board as long as we’re here. We each receive a room here at the War Hammer. [[Deanira]] takes the pouch and he tells us to turn it inside out on the bed. We ask him what he knows about the [[Murderhorn]] region. He says it’s very mountainous, and a half elf and his son came through a few months ago wanting

chunks.heading: Session 8 — 18 June 2025
chunks.text:
and his son came through a few months ago wanting to ski the region (our ghost friends who asked us to find their bodies and put them to rest). A lot of people go up but don’t come back, especially due to the weather, which make maps and charts quite useless, as mountain passes close from the wind and snow.
We go up to the rooms and [[Deanira]] turns the sack inside out on her bed. Three sacks fall out along with 3 greater healing potions. In each sack is 300 gold. We received this for providing the city [[Court]] with information about the mines.

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> In [[Tryborne Pass]] they find a slaughtered caravan and fight ravens and dire wolves. The ghost of [[Oswald]] leads them to [[Unfinished Business]], a tavern for lingering souls, and asks them to tell [[Mary Salter]] of his death. Elzock is returned to the [[Ring of Gold]].


We leave the [[Black Dragon Inn]] at 11 am to head back towards [[Truemetal Halls]]. As we travel along the mountainous canyon [[Tryborne Pass]], we hear a cacophony of ravens around a curve in the distance. [[Furgus]] sneaks ahead and looks around the curve. He sees bashed carts and Cuban fedora hat

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
e curve. He sees bashed carts and Cuban fedora hats surrounded by ravens picking at the bodies of the Cubans. We approach carefully and investigate the method in which the animals and Cubans were slain. They are covered in arrows and the occasional slashes.
[[Furgus]] notices that the arrows are larger than the ones you’d typically see. As we approach one of the carts to investigate it, the ravens attack. After a few rounds, the ravens are scared off by 3 approaching dire wolves, who are lured to us by the smell of blood. They attack. After defeating the dire wolves, we rummage through the car

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
eating the dire wolves, we rummage through the carts and find the oxen butchered with all of the choice cuts taken. On one of the bodies shielding a dead teenaged boy is a bloodstained note (on the following page).
We move on out of the canyon and find ourselves into a forest with a fog rolling in as the evening falls. It’s strange that the fog is rolling in at this time of day, and something about this feels very unnatural. Along the edge of the forest, [[Deanira]] sees a ghostly silhouette of the dead Cuban. [[Oswald]] from the note. He beckons for us to follow, and [[Deanira]] prances after

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
ns for us to follow, and [[Deanira]] prances after him. He leads her 100 yards off the trail, and we come across a building. The house looks beautiful from one angle and decrepit from another. When it’s decrepit, the sign above it says the “[[First Star]],” and when it’s pristine, the sign reads “[[Unfinished Business]].” As soon as we cross the threshold, the environment changes. Where it looked rotten and derelict before, it transforms into a lively tavern. 3 individuals are sitting and a bartender is cleaning Glasses. He hollers out to us, “Ah, we have three live ones!” We are welcomed
in t

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
Ah, we have three live ones!” We are welcomed
in to [[Unfinished Business]], the Business for wayfaring souls that aren’t ready to pass on. The bartender introduces himself as [[Anton]]. He was killed in a bar fight the first night he opened his bar. Now he caters to wandering souls. They never know where or when the bar will appear to mortals. The three other people are [[Oswald]], an older half orc dressed in plate, and a young half elf in the equivalent of his early 20s. [[Deanira]] approaches [[Oswald]] to speak to him. Dhruv talks to the half elf and [[WISC]] talks to the half orc in plat

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
alf elf and [[WISC]] talks to the half orc in plate. [[Oswald]] says [[Mary Salter]] is in [[Lakeshire]], his hometown. He asks [[Deanira]] to send her word (write) of his and their son’s passing. He said they were ambushed by huge bald humanoids with tattoos firing arrows. They then repelled down and finished them off with axes and swords. He asks for us to avenge him and his son, then use a courier to send word to Mary in [[Lakeshire]]. Their goods included salted fish, cigars, and fine rum.
NOTE: the dead have no sense of time. We can wait to do these quests. We may not even necessarily be

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
o do these quests. We may not even necessarily be the proper level for these quests yet.
Refer to the Quests page for details.
We are offered lodging for the night. When we wake up in the morning, we find ourselves on the forest floor, the tavern vanishing overnight. We continue on our way to [[Truemetal Halls]], and come across a berg, a single space that is heavily fortified and food is stored where a town will band together in the winter for protection. It’s the time of the year where the bergs are being prepared for when winter comes.
We drop off [[Elzock Emberstone]] at the [[Ring of Gold

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text:
op off [[Elzock Emberstone]] at the [[Ring of Gold]] to return him to his family.
We’re not let into the neighbourhood, so we’re promised payment and head to [[The Warhammer]]. We sit at the bar and tell [[Gunther Rockhammer]] of our travels. He pays us and tells us to stick around because there may be someone in the city who wants to talk to us. He gives us a room on the house and we level up.
A new shop has opened up in [[Truemetal Halls]] called [[The Shooting Star]], buys and sells magical items - Rupert Bubblegum
Backstory
[[Deanira]] was born in a coastal village where the tides were str

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text: born in a coastal village where the tides were strange and the stars never matched the charts. She didn’t have parents in particular, the culture of the tribe was that the children were raised by the whole community, not just by one or two. She was very close to a kind man named [[Val]], who was a handsome and gruff satyr in his late 40s/early 50s. She would sit with him and look over his shoulder as a small child and watch him draw exquisite maps. He taught her some cartography skills over the years. He would vanish over the horizon now and then, to chart what was beyond the line, especially

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text: en, to chart what was beyond the line, especially looking for this floating island whose position eternally changed and no map could hold. If you charted it on a map, the marking on the map would vanish as well. Some of the villagers thought he was mad, but [[Deanira]] thought he could see what no one else could. He was convinced that there were ruins on the island that would explain the origin of the world and why the stars change. One day he never came back. It’s taken everything in [[Deanira]] to hold herself back from sailing off to find him and his island. Everyone insisted that she drop

chunks.heading: Session 7 — 1 June 2025
chunks.text: m and his island. Everyone insisted that she drop the subject or the island would drive her mad, like it had to someone each generation. Now she’s honing her map making skills by travelling the Icemoor mountains and charting ruins, so that one day she may become skilled enough to find that island, and maybe find him too.

chunks.heading: Session 6 — 2 May 2025
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> WISC and Furgus reveal dreams in which Abbathor offered protection (Furgus signed in blood). Freed bugbear Crez guides them to the [[Black Dragon Inn]], where [[Hilda]] can't identify the stone.


[[WISC]] pulls the three of us into a huddle. When we were in the temple to Abathor, when we went to sleep, he woke up in a dream of a grand hall and Abathor was there. He told him we’d wake up and encounter 20+ armed soldiers. He said he’d protect us if [[WISC]] agreed to give out a handful of coins to people back in [[Truemetal Halls]]. Then [[Furgus]] says he had a very simila

chunks.heading: Session 6 — 2 May 2025
chunks.text:
Halls]]. Then [[Furgus]] says he had a very similar dream where Abathor gave the same info, but even though [[Furgus]] didn’t agree to do a favour, he had to sign a contract with Abathor with his blood anyway. [[WISC]] didn’t have to do this.
One of the Bugbears we freed from slavery is named Crez. He comes to us and says that he’s been looking around and thinks he knows where we are. In the distance, he points out columns of clouds rising into the sky. He says, “if I’m not mistaken, those are the hot springs outside of the [[Black Dragon Inn]]. The inn owner there offers training and supplies

chunks.heading: Session 6 — 2 May 2025
chunks.text:
. The inn owner there offers training and supplies. We could rest and resupply and then make our way back. Canborg road will take us to [[Truemetal Halls]]. The road is a major road that runs from [[Lakeshire]] to [[Truemetal Halls]]. As we part ways, Crez apologizes for not having anything to give to thank us. He says that if we ever find ourselves in the hamlet of Briar Run, we will have their hospitality.
We make our way to the [[Black Dragon Inn]]. The Inn itself is a beautiful Tudor style building. On the building are black dragon wings unfurled. They look remarkably preserved. As we appr

chunks.heading: Session 6 — 2 May 2025
chunks.text:
furled. They look remarkably preserved. As we approach the door, it opens for us. We don’t see any horses or carts outside. We enter and see well weathered tables. Chairs surrounding a table pull out for us. We see a sign by the bar that reads, “first drink’s free with a story”. [[WISC]] asks, “didn’t Cruz say that a woman named [[Hilda]] runs this place?” With that, we hear a voice from the back calling, “go ahead and take a seat!” When we sit, menus float to us.
A Halfling with curly gray hair floats out on a Tenzer’s Floating Disk. Both of her legs are missing from the knees down. She comes

chunks.heading: Session 6 — 2 May 2025
chunks.text:
er legs are missing from the knees down. She comes over and asks for a story in exchange for a round of drinks. We tell her the story of the possessed goat. We show her the stone and she is very interested. She pulls out her spellbook and casts Identify. She says, “interesting. Nothing comes up when I cast Identify.” We ask about the dragon wings. “He got my legs, but I got his wings.”
We spend our time in the hot springs where steam mephits cater to us along with more unseen servants. We ask [[Hilda]] if she recognizes the dagger symbol of Abathor. She does not specialize in religion. We go b

chunks.heading: Session 6 — 2 May 2025
chunks.text:
thor. She does not specialize in religion. We go back to the bar and as the day grows later, we see the bar filling up with various species including Cubans. A Dwarven woman recognizes [[Elzock Emberstone]] and comes over. They go off and chat. He later lets us know that they’re “business acquaintances”. She has done business with the family in the past.
[[Deanira]] spends her evening playing a rapid and dexterous game of cards. [[WISC]] gambles at a game of “In Between”. We wake up the next morning at 11am, having been thrown off by weeks in the darkness and drinks from the night before.

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> They escape by water breathing past a water weird and free six captives, including [[Elzock Emberstone]]. A dead Halfling adventurer's coded journal yields the word **Axeholm**, and they emerge into daylight.


We awaken to the sounds of many Dwarven voices approaching the lake. We’re still in the hallway where we went to sleep, and [[WISC]] wakes up to find a scroll and a pouch of coins next to him. He cracks open the door and while he doesn’t see anyone, he hears angry voices. The one phrase that he can make out is, “find them”. [[WISC]] looks at the scroll and only he s

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text: them”. [[WISC]] looks at the scroll and only he sees writing on it. It is a scroll of water breathing. We decide to hide underwater. [[WISC]] can somehow read these runes only he can see, despite being illiterate. He reads aloud the incantation and we head into the dark cool water. We feel a slight current heading down and under the temple. We dive down and follow it. We see blind fish swimming, but no vegetation. As we approach the wall, we see a hole carved into it, just big enough for people. We swim through and it opens into a cavern pool, like an air pocket chamber. As [[Deanira]] surfac

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text: like an air pocket chamber. As [[Deanira]] surfaces, [[Furgus]] feels the water around him tighten up and grapple him. [[Deanira]] comes back underwater and sees [[Furgus]] struggling and fighting against something invisible. She pierces a spot near [[Furgus]] with a mithril dagger and feels a sort of resistance, like the water is taking the blow. We all attack the entity, [[Deanira]] remembers it to be a water weird. Once we kill it, we continue through the hole on the other side. We surface in the next chamber and see a shore and natural stone steps leading up to a crack in the stone. We sh

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text: ne steps leading up to a crack in the stone. We shimmy through and find ourselves in a tunnel stretching to our right and left. As we stand there, the water dripping off of us onto the ground flows down the tunnel to our right. We head to the left tunnel that slopes up slightly. We walk for a long time. We eventually settle down after about 8 hours of walking. [[Deanira]] maps out where they’ve been so far, and they are still heading further away from the edge of the map we were given. During the night, we hear subtle sounds of work going on down the tunnel, very far off. The next day, we cont

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text:
wn the tunnel, very far off. The next day, we continue on. Eventually we come to an offshoot. We can either continue down the
main tunnel or explore this offshoot. We continue up the main tunnel for the better part of a day. [[Deanira]] begins to hear more sounds above, though still too distant to make out what they are. We continue on until we can hear more clearly. We hear a curse in Undercommon and a squeal, like someone was hit. We look around for places to hide. We see fissures in the rock and overhangs we could hide in. [[Deanira]] squeezes into a fissure and [[WISC]] climbs onto an over

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text: es into a fissure and [[WISC]] climbs onto an overhang. [[Furgus]] tries to climb up onto an overhang but the rock buckles and he falls spread-eagled onto the cave floor and the noise of rock falling around him echoes through the cave. We roll initiative. [[Deanira]] misty steps behind the group and waits to attack from behind. They eventually turn around to go back and see her, and we all attack. One younger attacker runs and gets away. We continue up the tunnel. Not too far up, we see half a dozen people rope-bound in the tunnel. We tell them we’re friends and take off their hoods. We ask th

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text:
we’re friends and take off their hoods. We ask them what happened. All of them have been down here a few days. One of the Dwarves ([[Elzock Emberstone]]) says that if we can get them to [[Truemetal Halls]], he can make it worth our while. His family lives in the Golden Circle there (the fancy homes up high in the grand chamber entering [[Truemetal Halls]]). We give them rations and spare arms.
They are farmers, not fighters, but they look more intimidating armed. We walk for the rest of the day, then settle down for the night, planning to finish the journey out tomorrow. The following day we

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text: sh the journey out tomorrow. The following day we come upon a Y intersection. The one to the right seems more highly trafficked, but to the left we hear the faint sound of birds and a slight breeze of fresh air. We follow this one. We emerge into a large cavern. Looking up, we see the sky, with sunlight streaming down on our faces for the first time in days. Looking around, we see a rope hanging down from the lip of the chamber. It stops 60-70 ft above the ground and the end is frayed. On the ground we see the body of a Halfling and the rest of the rope. We search the body and find a journal o

chunks.heading: Session 5 — 18 April 2025
chunks.text:
the rope. We search the body and find a journal on him, written in common, but seemingly in code. The guy was an adventurer like us, trying to find archaeological
locations to unearth wealth. [[Furgus]] has a background in archaeology, and investigates the journal. One word stands out and is written in Dwarvish: [[Axeholm]]. None of us have ever heard the word before. This beautiful area doesn’t offer any new paths, so we turn back to check out the other tunnel. At the end of the tunnel is a fake wall that can be pushed. We push through and emerge into the grass and sunlight.

chunks.heading: Session 4 — 9 March 2025
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> At the bottom they ambush Duergar hauling ore and spot a large Duergar smelting compound worked by slaves. Across an underground lake, a blood-opened door leads to a temple of [[Abbathor]], where they kill an evil priestess.


At the base is a pile of ore. 3 paths lead from the cavern, one forward, one left, one right. The rock around us is covered in slightly bioluminescent lichen, providing dim light. We hear the sounds of wheels and voices approaching. The three of us dash partway into a dark tunnel to hide. Four Dwarvish looking individuals clad heavily in armour emerg

chunks.heading: Session 4 — 9 March 2025
chunks.text: h looking individuals clad heavily in armour emerge with a Bugbear pulling the cart. [[Furgus]] recognises them as Duergar. They are permanently underground dwelling, and were not represented by the clan statues in the city, as they are not considered true Dwarves. There has been conflict between the Dwarves and Duergar for millennia. They pull up to the pile of ore and the Bugbear begins loading it into the cart. When they enter the tunnel we’re hiding in, we attack them. The Bugbear dies at the hands of one of the Duergar. On them we find that each has a lead pendant of a dagger painted to l

chunks.heading: Session 4 — 9 March 2025
chunks.text:
t each has a lead pendant of a dagger painted to look like gold. Perhaps a clan or holy symbol. We decide to sneak down the tunnel they came from to see what their operation is. After 1-2 miles of tunnel, it opens into
a larger cavern space. We see about 20 Duergar and an array of other humanoids that are their enslaved. It appears to be some sort of compound where they are smelting the ore. We decide to go back and check out the other tunnels to get more of an idea of what’s around here and how it’s all connected. We hear footsteps behind us and fight another group of 4 when we get back to th

chunks.heading: Session 4 — 9 March 2025
chunks.text: nd fight another group of 4 when we get back to the first chamber. It’s very close, but we win the battle. We go to rest in the less travelled tunnel and rest while [[Furgus]] scouts ahead. He comes across an underground lake with a gravel beach on the far side with a rowboat and a stone door. He comes back and tells [[WISC]] and [[Deanira]] about the lake and the stone door. After a little rest, we make our way to the lake to check it out. We get to the lake and swim to the other side unimpeded. We have a feeling that the reason we got across just fine is because we picked up the Duergar pend

chunks.heading: Session 4 — 9 March 2025
chunks.text: just fine is because we picked up the Duergar pendants. We land on the beach and approach the stone door, with the same stone dagger symbol as the amulets. [[Furgus]] nicks his finger with an arrow and offers his blood to the door. The door absorbs it and opens. There is a small foyer with braziers and a hallway leading to an altar displaying a large jewelled dagger made of actual gold and gems. On the altar itself is the body of a Knocker. We put on our medallions and walk in. We go down to the altar and see that the Knocker’s heart is carved out, but there is no blood on the altar itself. [[

chunks.heading: Session 4 — 9 March 2025
chunks.text: out, but there is no blood on the altar itself. [[WISC]] recognises this symbol as that of Abbathor, the Dwarven god of greed. He is seen to most Dwarves as a curse more so than a blessing; he has also been known to induce madness. A voice comes from the darkness, “You three will make great sacrifices to him.” We fight an evil priest of Abbathor. After we kill her, we long rest in the chamber with her body.

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text:
> [!summary] TL;DR
> Exploring the sealed mine, the party fights shadow Dwarves, gricks and a gelatinous cube, and recovers goggles of night from two dead Halfling miners. Beyond the cave-in they find Knockers mining mithril for "The Great One" and jump down the chute to meet his priests.


The slam of the doors echoes through the vast chambers of the cave. Somewhere in the distance we hear damp drips bathed in the silence. [[Deanira]] lights the lantern and Wisk leads the way. We make our way down the first hall and at the end we notice something shifting on the far wall. It appears to be mov

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text:
ing shifting on the far wall. It appears to be moving shadows of two Dwarves. [[Deanira]] calls out a Dwarvish greeting tentatively. They attack. Once we dispose of the shadows, we continue on. After another few hours, we go down an offshoot and enter a large rounded open area. In the middle, we find a pile of what seems like gelatin. Upon inspection, [[Deanira]] and [[Furgus]] get the impression that they are like a mix of amphibian eggs and reptile eggs, encased in jelly to preserve their moisture. As [[Deanira]] looks around the room,
she sees 5 different holes that could hold a medium crea

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text: es 5 different holes that could hold a medium creature each. We feel a rumble. 2 gricks pop out of the burrows and instantly down [[WISC]]. One of the the gricks brings [[Deanira]] down to her last hit point with one critical strike. She falls to her knees. As it moves to slither back into its burrow, she whips out her hand and grabs it by the neck and chokes it. [[Furgus]] shoots the last one down the throat. We stomp the remaining eggs. We go back to a more familiar part of the mine and make camp. When we turn down the lamps, we are immersed in the greatest darkness we’ve ever experienced. W

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text: in the greatest darkness we’ve ever experienced. While keeping watch, [[WISC]] hears the faintest sound of picks hitting ore, though he can’t be sure. In the morning, we make our way further into the cave. Eventually a large chasm blocks our path through the tunnel. [[WISC]] drops a torch down into it to judge the depth, but the flame sputters out before he even lets go of it. He remembers the warning we received before the doors closed, that if our flames go out, we’re entering an area devoid of oxygen. We look down into it with our lanterns and barely make out two Halfling bodies at the bott

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text:
nd barely make out two Halfling bodies at the bottom.
They are both wearing goggles, and that’s when we remember that Halflings don’t have darkvision. We lower [[WISC]] down the 15 ft necessary and retrieve the goggles. We know the mineshaft was closed 20 years ago, but the bodies do not show significant signs of decomposition. We attribute this to the lack of oxygen down in the chasm. One of the Halfling miners has a tattoo that reads “I like to get dirty in dark holes”. On the miners we find lamp oil and a bullseye lantern, a hooded lantern, and two pairs of goggles of night. We make our way

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text:
and two pairs of goggles of night. We make our way on for a little while and find a Barracks.
We camp there for the night, and [[Deanira]] spends the evening deconstructing the goggles of night and inserting them into her ritual deer skull mask. Several days later as we’re exploring a chamber, a big gelatinous cube drops from the ceiling and barely misses us. We fight it to clear the mine. We make our way to the area where the massive cave-in happened. Eerily, we can tell that there are mining sounds again…on the other side. According to the map, there shouldn’t be any space beyond this. [[WIS

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text:
p, there shouldn’t be any space beyond this. [[WISC]] and
[[Furgus]] notice a hole that has been tunnelled through the cave-in. [[WISC]] peaks in and sees that it continues on for a long time. This tunnel is messily carved, nothing close to the level of the Dwarven. This was someone else. Someone else who has moved in to resume mining operations down here. We sneak into the tunnel and make our way quietly towards the noise. Eventually it opens up into a larger chamber, the ceiling reinforced with timber. We see eight Tiny creatures working away with pick axes and wheelbarrows. They empty the w

chunks.heading: Session 3 — 29 February 2025
chunks.text:
with pick axes and wheelbarrows. They empty the wheelbarrows down the mining shaft. We walk into the room and fan out. We talk to them and learn that they’re the Knockers. They are mining the mithril to make weapons so they can expand and take over all of the mine on behalf of The Great One.
The priests of the Great One are apparently at the bottom of the chute. They tell us to go down to the chute to meet the Great One. We jump down the chute.

chunks.heading: Source Notes
chunks.text:
**Original source:** `Icemoor Mountains copy.docx`

This vault is a structured transformation of the campaign notes. The source contains 80 pages and records at least 36 numbered sessions, plus campaign setup, backstory, quests, and miscellaneous notes.

chunks.heading: Data-model choices
chunks.text:
- Characters/NPCs → `People/`
- Settlements/regions/locations → `Places/`
- Organizations → `Factions/`
- Important objects → `Items/`
- Plot hooks → `Quests/`
- Unresolved investigations → `Clues & Mysteries/`
- Worldbuilding/reference facts → `Lore/`
- Play-by-play records → `Sessions/`

chunks.heading: Canon / uncertainty
chunks.text:
The original notes contain inconsistent spellings and occasional uncertain names. Those are preserved through aliases or separate reference notes where practical.

Examples:
- [[Talir Rengavi]] / Tallir / Talir
- [[Christolf Nightfall]] / Kristoff / Kristof
- [[Venburg]] / Venberg
- [[Kriptin Forest]] / Krypton Forest
- [[Tryborne Pass]] / Triborn Pass
- [[Savehaven]] / Safehaven (possibly the same port; unconfirmed)
- [[Peter Owens]] / Peter Owen
- [[Klaus]] / Claus
- [[Wren Nalore]]
- [[Zyuir]]

When the notes explicitly express uncertainty, this vault does not silently convert it into certa

chunks.text: this vault does not silently convert it into certainty.

chunks.heading: Werebear Curse
chunks.text: **Status:** resolved

chunks.heading: Objective
chunks.text: Cure [[WISC]] and [[Furgus]] after their wounds failed to heal following the Stone Giant were-bear encounter. [[Bianca Onyxcrest]] arranged magical treatment.

chunks.heading: Clues & findings
chunks.text:
The party fought Stone Giant were-bears near [[Hawk's Nest]]. [[WISC]] and [[Furgus]] later discovered that their bite wounds were not healing.

Notes establish:
- Lycanthropy can be acquired through a bite.
- A first full moon creates a critical deadline for conventional cures.
- A [[Wolfsbane Potion]] may be possible.
- Possible ingredients include wolfsbane, a stabilizing agent, powdered moonstone/moon seed, lycanthrope blood, and purified/blessed water.
- [[Bianca Onyxcrest]] eventually agreed to arrange magical treatment.

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text: - [[Session 37]]: [[WISC]] and [[Furgus]] were cured of lycanthropy at the [[Temple of Mistra]] by [[Samuel Patel]].

chunks.text: Identify the golden-eyed bugbear who terrorized [[Copperhead Hollow]] and determine whether they are related to [[WISC]].

chunks.text:
[[WISC]] shares a rare eye colour with another bugbear encountered indirectly.

[[Jane Pedimore]] reported that a golden-eyed bugbear had extorted protection payments from her family near [[Copperhead Hollow]]. When they refused, her brother, father, and grandfather were killed.

The party suspects this bugbear may be related to WISC.

chunks.heading: Gauntlet
chunks.text:
**Status:** upcoming

Competition at [[Mistra's Academy]] in [[Amberhold]]. The party will compete on behalf of the [[Library of Deneir]], and has also been asked to represent the Academy. Kicked off by the [[Academy Gala]].

chunks.heading: Rules (from [[Bianca Onyxcrest]], [[Session 36]])
chunks.text:
- 5 bouts against creatures. Teams compete independently, not against each other.
- A prize is awarded at the end of each bout.
- About 10–15 minutes between bouts while the arenas reset.
- One short rest allowed across the 5 bouts (via the Cat Nap spell).
- Clerics on hand revive anyone who falls, but a member revived by them is out for the remaining bouts. A member revived by their own party can keep fighting.

chunks.heading: Known details ([[Session 38]])
chunks.text:
[[Riffle]] glimpsed these in [[Karyn]]'s office:
- Four teams in total.
- Five themed rounds: Beasts, Celestials, Fiends, Elementals, and Fey.

chunks.heading: Daggins Murder
chunks.text: **Status:** active

chunks.heading: Objective
chunks.text: Determine who murdered [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]], stole his Axeholm research, and attempted to frame [[Riffle]].

chunks.heading: Clues & findings
chunks.text:
[[Daddy Dildo Daggins]] was found dead in his study with a knife in his back. His blood appeared to spell `RI` followed by part of an `F`.

Black feathers surrounded the body, and a witness claimed someone resembling [[Riffle]] entered the house wearing red vestments.

The party determined:
- The feathers were ordinary bird feathers, not Kenku feathers.
- Red Library robes had been discontinued/destroyed about 20 years ago.
- Someone had purchased unusually small black raven feathers from a fletcher.
- Daggins's Axeholm research disappeared.
- [[Sherlock Gnomes]] believes someone was trying to

chunks.heading: Clues & findings
chunks.text: [[Sherlock Gnomes]] believes someone was trying to impersonate and frame Riffle.

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text:
- [[Session 37]]: [[Ester]] dates the change from red to purple robes to **50–60 years ago**, not about 20 years as recorded above. The source notes conflict, so both are kept. She also says some people may have kept their old robes, so the red-robed figure need not be Library staff.
- [[Session 38]]: Daggins was "Brother Daggins" of the [[Union of Many]].
- [[Session 38]]: Riffle is again accused of a theft on the word of a witness. See [[Talir's Stolen Documents]].

chunks.heading: Anthracite Trade Mystery
chunks.text: **Status:** active

chunks.heading: Objective
chunks.text: Determine why [[Black Hand Dwarves]] doubled the price of [[Anthracite]] and whether another buyer is secretly purchasing it.

chunks.heading: Clues & findings
chunks.text:
[[Anthracite]] is essential for forging [[Mithril]] and adamantine. The [[Black Hand Dwarves]] unexpectedly doubled its price despite historically stable pricing.

This suggests they may have another buyer or are diverting supply.

**Potential links:** [[Kohlemine]], [[Black Hand Dwarves]], [[Truemetal Halls]], [[Mithril]], [[Axeholm]].

chunks.heading: Academy Gala
chunks.text:
**Status:** upcoming

Gala at [[Mistra's Academy]] to show off the stone from the belly of the ram (the [[Mystery Stone]]) and to kick off the [[Gauntlet]]. It is drawing many alumni donations and much scholarly interest. The party has been asked to represent both the Academy and the [[Library of Deneir]].

[[Agatha]]'s porridge tasted to Deanira like her favourite fish dish from Coda's Landing ([[Session 21]]).

chunks.heading: Amberhold
chunks.text: Major southern city and home of [[Riffle]]'s [[Library of Deneir]], [[Mistra's Academy]], the Mage's District, and the upcoming [[Gauntlet]].

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text:
- [[Session 37]]: A [[Sect of Torm]] has been attacking alcohol shops. The city job board offers the [[Missing Sanitation Workers]] job and a suspicious scholarship flyer (see [[Blond Skeletal Hand Recruiter]]).
- [[Session 37]]–38: New locations include the [[Temple of Mistra]], the [[Temple of the Raven Queen]], and the [[Owens Family Mausoleum]] in the graveyard to the west.
- [[Session 39]]: The [[Owens Warehouse]] on the riverfront docks hides Peter Owens's laboratory, reached by a teleporting crest in the family crypt.

chunks.heading: Ambercrown Kingdom
chunks.text: Kingdom ruled by King Xavier, who took the throne shortly before its war with the [[Dragon League]] about 15–20 years ago. The war lasted only a few months and the Dragon League lost ([[Session 36]]). This year the King's birthday coincides with the Harvest Moon festival, making for a bigger celebration in [[Amberhold]] ([[Session 24]]).

chunks.heading: Admiral's Point
chunks.text: Place with an island to its south, home to a holy pool tended by a religious order of [[Sune]] ([[Session 34]]). One of three blessed-water sites for a [[Wolfsbane Potion]].

chunks.heading: WISC
chunks.text:
**Role:** Player character  
**Species:** Bugbear

chunks.heading: Known history
chunks.text:
- WISC's father left before WISC was a baby.
- WISC grew up around [[Venburg]] and [[Oma]].
- A rare eye colour links WISC to another golden-eyed bugbear.
- A woman from [[Copperhead Hollow]] reported a golden-eyed bugbear extorting protection taxes and murdering her family. She initially believed WISC was that bugbear.

chunks.heading: Important relationships
chunks.text:
- [[Furgus]] — long-time adventuring companion.
- [[Deanira]] — party member.
- [[Riffle]] — party member; often suspicious of WISC.
- [[Oma]] — grandmother.
- [[Uthal]] — former enemy/ally whose history became entangled with WISC's family.

chunks.heading: Items / notable events
chunks.text:
- Uses the [[Grey Bag of Tricks]].
- Received [[Reaper]] from the Emberstone family.
- Was affected by the [[Werebear Curse]].
- Has repeatedly interacted with [[Cornhusk Dolls]].

chunks.heading: Open threads
chunks.text:
- Identity and origin of the golden-eyed bugbear.
- WISC's missing father.
- Whether the golden-eyed bugbear is related to WISC.

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text:
- [[Session 37]]: Cured of lycanthropy at the [[Temple of Mistra]] ([[Werebear Curse]]).
- [[Session 39]]: Lifted the sarcophagus lids and rescued [[Riffle]] and [[Deanira]], and found the fake wooden sarcophagus hiding the crypt ladder. His socks are Peter's gag.

chunks.text:
**Role:** Player character  
**Species:** Kenku  
**Class:** Cleric of [[Deneir]]

chunks.text:

- [[Hana Goldfirm]] is Riffle's close friend/researcher.

chunks.heading: Backstory
chunks.text: Riffle serves as a clandestine collector of knowledge, artifacts, and secrets for the Library. During a past journey with Talir, a fire injured Riffle while they rescued Talir. Riffle describes the burn as the price paid to become a cleric.

chunks.heading: Major threads
chunks.text:
- [[Axeholm]]
- [[Skeletal Hand]]
- [[Master of Death]]
- [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]]
- [[Mystery Stone]]
- Suspicion that the conspiracy may involve [[Amberhold]], [[Mistra's Academy]], or the [[Library of Deneir]] itself.

chunks.heading: Notes
chunks.text: Riffle is highly inquisitive, prone to theft and mischief, and has accumulated a substantial number of secrets.

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text:
- [[Session 37]]: Asked [[Talir Rengavi]] to read the scholarship flyer. Talir thought Riffle was admitting they couldn't read and apologised for being a "bad" father; the misunderstanding was cleared up.
- [[Session 37]]: Learned of the [[Sect of Torm]] attacks on alcohol shops.
- [[Session 37]]: Learned from [[Ester]] that the old red robes were changed to purple 50–60 years ago and some people may have kept theirs. The person seen at Daggins's murder wore red robes (see [[Daggins Murder]]).

vet Glove Brothel]], who described a blond young man named [[Andrew]].

- [[Session 38]]: Helped [[Karyn]] and glimpsed details of the [[Gauntlet]].
- [[Session 38]]: Accused by Talir, via Sending, of stealing documents from his safe. See [[Talir's Stolen Documents]].

chunks.heading: Peter Owens
chunks.text:
Graduate student at [[Mistra's Academy]] (School of Conjuration, per [[Session 36]]). Son of the late Lord Richard Owens, the merchant whose death has left a ship stuck in port because its cargo can't be unloaded into his warehouse.

The notes spell the family name both **Owens** ([[Session 36]]) and **Owen** ([[Session 38]]).

- [[Session 36]]: [[Riffle]] remembered the son's name only as "something with a P".

chunks.heading: Peter Owens
chunks.text:
mily Mausoleum]] more often, which they find strange because he wasn't close to his parents. They describe him as strange, with "icky weird vibes". He lives in an apartment off campus. See [[Owens Family Deaths]].

**Possible link (still unconfirmed after his capture):** the [[Skeletal Hand]] recruiter in [[Session 30]] was described as a blond youth named Peter. See [[Blond Skeletal Hand Recruiter]].

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text:
- [[Session 39]]: **Captured.** He had raised his parents, [[Richard Owens]] and [[Gezibel Owens]], as greater zombies and called on them to attack the party in his laboratory under the [[Owens Warehouse]]. [[Furgus]] shot him with an [[Arrow of the Harpy]], charming him into a stupor; the party destroyed the zombies, and they tied Peter up and gagged him with WISC's socks.
- [[Session 39]]: His notes name [[Deanira]] and [[Coda's Landing]] as a target, and say he "needs a female phase". See [[Peter's Experiments]].

chunks.heading: Deanira
chunks.text:
**Role:** Player character  
**Species:** Satyr

chunks.heading: Backstory
chunks.text:
Deanira was raised communally in a coastal village where tides were strange and the stars did not match the charts. She was close to [[Val]], an older satyr cartographer who searched for a mysterious floating island whose position constantly changed. Val believed ruins there could explain the origin of the world and the changing stars. Val eventually disappeared.

Deanira now travels the Icemoor region, improving her cartography skills and searching for clues to the island and Val.

chunks.text:

- Has repeatedly encountered [[Cornhusk Dolls]].
- Was bitten by the were-bears but did not develop the same persistent symptoms as WISC/Furgus.

- [[Session 37]]: Bought maps of four other continents from a cartography shop. The shop had charted nothing in the Feywild and knew nothing of an unchartable island, so she questioned sailors (see [[Floating Island Mystery]]).
- [[Session 37]]: Wants to continue Daggins's work collecting fertility statues from around the world.
- [[Session 38]]: Met the [[Union of Many]] in the basement of [[The Two Tits]] a

chunks.heading: Wolfsbane Potion
chunks.text:
Campaign recipe notes:

- Wolfsbane
- Stabilizing agent (holy water, belladonna, etc.)
- Powdered moonstone or moon seed
- Blood of a lycanthrope
- Purified water or water from a blessed body of water

Potential blessed-water locations:
- [[Kriptin Forest]]
- [[Amberhold]] — cared for by the sisters of Lethander
- An island south of [[Admiral's Point]] under the care of a religious order of [[Sune]]

chunks.heading: Tiamat
chunks.text: Dragon goddess worshipped by the [[Dragon League]], whose blessing let them control dragons. About 100 years ago she was put down in a battle among the gods, and the League lost that power ([[Session 36]]).

chunks.heading: Sune
chunks.text: Deity whose religious order tends a holy pool on an island south of [[Admiral's Point]] ([[Session 34]]).

chunks.heading: Raven Queen
chunks.text:
[[Theo'din Corvis]] serves the Raven Queen and describes her as strongly opposed to necromancy.

Theo's personal history involves a bargain his mother made with the Raven Queen to save her life, at the cost of one of her twins.

chunks.heading: Recent developments
chunks.text:
- [[Session 37]]: Theo communed with her ("the Matron") at the [[Temple of the Raven Queen]]. She appeared as a woman in a white mask, a black dress, and a cloak of raven feathers.

%% session-history:start %%

chunks.heading: Session history
chunks.text:
> [!info]- 2 sessions · first [[Session 32]] · last [[Session 37]]
> - [[Session 32]]: Theo'din Corvis’din reveals that his patron is the Raven Queen, who is very anti-necromancy.
> - [[Session 37]]: They suggest that he reach out to the Raven Queen and ask her himself (through prayer).
%% session-history:end %%

chunks.heading: Mithril
chunks.text: Precious metal mined and forged in the north. The Knockers and [[Duergar]] were mining it to arm a force ([[Session 03]], [[Session 08]]). Working it requires [[Anthracite]]. The poisonous [[Miner's Death Lode]] was a mithril mine.

chunks.heading: Lord of Fire
chunks.text: One of the [[Lords of the Elements]]. It was defeated in the western volcanic region now home to the [[Fire Dwarves]], frozen into obsidian and shattered. The [[Mystery Stone]] is one of its fragments ([[Session 24]]).

chunks.heading: Ligos
chunks.text: Name of the world (or continent) where elementals ran rampant about 3,000 years ago, before the [[Elementalist Syndicate]] bound them ([[Session 24]]).

chunks.heading: Glabrezu
chunks.text: Demon guarding the desecrated mountaintop temple where [[Balgus]] lies. See [[Warrior of Kord]].

chunks.heading: Flame Skull
chunks.text: Undead the party destroyed in the sunken Dragon Cult fortress ([[Session 20]]). Its ashes would reanimate, so they sealed them in the [[Unbreakable Vial]], later traded to [[Agatha]] ([[Session 21]]). Riffle's journal copies burned in this fight ([[Session 36]]).

chunks.heading: Deneir
chunks.text:
God associated in the notes with scribes, knowing, writing, books, and knowledge.

[[Riffle]] is a cleric of Deneir and works for the [[Library of Deneir]].

chunks.heading: Cidis
chunks.text: Dragon in whose name the [[Cult of the Destroyer]] ruled, taxed and mined. Cidis vanished about 800 years ago, after which the cult was overthrown and its dam broken, turning the forest into bog ([[Session 17]]).

chunks.heading: Anthracite
chunks.text: Extremely hard coal that burns hot enough, for long enough, to forge [[Mithril]] and adamantine. It is mined only by the [[Black Hand Dwarves]] at [[Kohlemine]]. Its price suddenly doubled ([[Session 10]], [[Session 17]]). See [[Anthracite Trade Mystery]].

chunks.heading: Abbathor
chunks.text:
Dwarven god of greed. In the notes, Abbathor is viewed by many Dwarves more as a curse than a blessing and is associated with madness.

The party encountered an underground temple with an Abbathor symbol while investigating the [[Duergar]] mining operation.

chunks.heading: Unbreakable Vial
chunks.text:
Small glass vial demonstrated to be extremely resistant to damage. Used to contain the ashes of a [[Flame Skull]].

chunks.heading: Union of Many
chunks.text: Religious order whose members follow many deities of fertility and love, including Shialliah, Lethander and Melorah. They emphasise open love, strong relationships within their community and across deity lines, and living life to the fullest. Their gatherings begin with a Zone of Truth and are restricted to those over 18.

chunks.text:
- [[Atheela]]
- [[Daddy Dildo Daggins]] ("Brother Daggins"). His collection of fertility statues from many cultures makes sense in this light.

This likely explains why [[The Vine's Bounty]] was boarded up with broken glass, and why [[Decanter 3 Table]] had a guard at the door ([[Session 36]]). That link is an inference.

chunks.text: Underground-dwelling Dwarves, not counted among the true Dwarven clans, in conflict with them for millennia. [[The Bastard's Band]] later disrupted them ([[Session 23]]).

chunks.heading: Dragon League
chunks.text:
Historical dragon-worshiping organization devoted to [[Tiamat]]. They could control dragons and used them in warfare.

The Dragon League fought the [[Ambercrown Kingdom]] around 15–20 years before the campaign. The notes also describe older Dragon League-related ruins containing:
- a dragon shrine
- a baptismal font
- dragon imagery
- a vault containing magical equipment
- documents and blackmail materials

The party recovered evidence that may connect ancient Dragon League activity to [[Axeholm]].
